clue.text: Not completely how steeples are built?

definitions.meaning: partly, to a limited degree, as in agreeing only in part
a steeple rises to a spire, so it is literally constructed to finish at a tip

explanation.surface: A wry question about church architecture, prefaced by a hedge.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means partially or to some extent, a qualified agreement rather than a full one.

clue.text: Terrier mine? Nonsense

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
bull is slang for rubbish or nonsense

explanation.surface: Someone claims a terrier belongs to them and is dismissed as talking nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' looks like a possessive but is the colliery noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed so named is a muscular fighting terrier, an example of the dog type.

clue.text: Just over 50 in New York

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over, a set of six balls

indicators.note: the numeral sits within the abbreviation for the city

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone is barely past fifty years old while living in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and only are synonyms meaning merely or no more than.

clue.text: Conditional release initially playing a part

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word playing

parts.note: an actor's part is a role

explanation.surface: An actor granted early release from prison on condition they play a part.
explanation.definitionFit: Parole is the early freeing of a prisoner subject to good behaviour, a release with conditions.

clue.text: Certain hat being used

indicators.note: used as in worn or second-hand, so the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is sure the hat is in use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' is the anagram signal on HAT BEING, whose eight letters rearrange into the three-word phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes an outcome as secured or assured, a sure thing.

clue.text: Under emotional strain in past, perhaps

definitions.meaning: past is one example of a grammatical verb form, like present or future

explanation.surface: Someone was stressed in the past.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is nervy and strained; the other is the grammar term for verb time, of which past is an example.

clue.text: Understand English teacher at university left later for the same place

definitions.text: left later for the same place

parts.note: to follow an argument is to understand it
a don is a university lecturer, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A university English teacher sets off later to the same destination.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a side made to bat again straight after its first innings is said to have done this, but here the definition is the plain going-after sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To go after someone towards the same destination is to set off behind them, a phrasal-verb description.

clue.text: Unnerve leader in rainforest, pointing to snake

parts.note: to rattle someone is to unnerve them

indicators.note: the leader in a word is its first letter, here of rainforest

explanation.surface: A guide in the jungle is frightened when someone points out a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattler is an informal name for a rattlesnake, a kind of venomous viper.

clue.text: Footballers here, very very enthusiastic, deliver

parts.note: real is informal for very, as in real good
mad about something is very keen on it
to rid is to deliver or free from something

explanation.surface: Fans of a team are urged, with great enthusiasm, to deliver a win.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'very' is not emphasis: the first gives REAL on its own, the second joins 'enthusiastic' for MAD.
explanation.definitionFit: This Spanish club is a famous football team, so its players are footballers.

clue.text: Dance beat good orchestra originally provides

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them

indicators.note: originally picks the opening letter of orchestra

explanation.surface: An orchestra plays a dance with a good rhythm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat' looks like musical rhythm but means thrash.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a ballroom dance from Argentina, an example of the category.

clue.text: A strange plant with arrow-shaped leaves

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A description of an odd-looking plant with pointed leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: The lily so named, such as cuckoo-pint, has distinctive arrowhead-shaped foliage.

clue.text: Buzzer on low woodland flower

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece on another follows it, so the buzzer comes after

parts.note: blue means low or depressed
a bell is a device that rings or buzzes

explanation.surface: An alarm in a low tone sounds over the woods.
explanation.definitionFit: This spring wildflower carpets British woods with blue blooms each April and May.

clue.text: So, Racine changed storyline

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are changed into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone rewrote a play by the French dramatist Racine.
explanation.walkthrough: Racine was a 17th-century French tragedian, which suits a plot being altered.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is the outline or plot of a film or play, a synonym for storyline.

clue.text: Married girl in spite

parts.note: Alice is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A woman married out of spite.
explanation.definitionFit: Spite and malice both mean a desire to harm or upset others.

clue.text: Contrivance used in ground-breaking public school

definitions.meaning: a farm implement with spikes or discs for breaking up ploughed soil
a famous English fee-paying school in north-west London

explanation.surface: A private school breaks ground on a new project.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a public school is an old private fee-paying school; Harrow, in north-west London, is among the best known.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the farming tool that breaks up clods; the other is the well-known school.

clue.text: Managed to risk incurring endless bitterness

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it, past tense ran

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the word for risk incurring is dropped

parts.note: to court danger is to risk incurring it

explanation.surface: Someone managed to provoke unending resentment.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is lasting resentment or bitterness, a close synonym.

clue.text: Friendly foreign correspondent, maybe

parts.note: a foreign correspondent sounds like a journalist abroad, but here it is a friend overseas who writes letters

explanation.surface: A description of an amiable overseas journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A friend made by exchanging letters, often living abroad, is exactly a friendly correspondent from another country.

clue.text: Activity outside called mad

indicators.note: the word for activity sits outside the word for called

parts.note: a deed is an act or activity
rang means called on the phone

explanation.surface: Someone outdoors shouted that a thing was crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Deranged means insane or crazy, a synonym of mad.

clue.text: Darts run by experts

indicators.note: by means beside, so the two pieces are placed next to each other

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
aces are experts

explanation.surface: A darts match organised by skilled players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Darts' looks like the pub game but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To dart and to race both mean to move quickly; darts here is a verb form.

clue.text: Girl teen idol embraces

indicators.note: the words teen idol hold the name within them

explanation.surface: A young woman hugs a pop star.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid is a girl's name, as in the author Enid Blyton.

clue.text: Stinging insect was on piano

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: An insect with a sting landed on a piano.
explanation.definitionFit: A wasp is a common yellow and black stinging insect.

clue.text: Suffer at home, remedy falling short

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: falling short means the word for remedy loses its last letter

parts.note: a cure is a remedy

explanation.surface: Someone ill at home finds their treatment fails to work.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a loss is to suffer it, a synonym in that sense.

clue.text: Squad also included in scheme

indicators.note: the word for also is placed within the word for scheme

parts.note: a plan is a scheme
too means also

explanation.surface: A team was part of the plan as well.
explanation.definitionFit: A platoon is a small military unit, a squad of soldiers.

clue.text: Booty found by harbour brings misery

indicators.note: found by means placed beside, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: spoils are booty or plunder
a port is a harbour

explanation.surface: Pirates' treasure discovered near a harbour causes unhappiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misery' looks like an abstract noun, but in British slang a misery is a gloomy person who dampens others' fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A misery, in informal British use, is a killjoy who spoils fun, a synonym.
